title: Noisy-tenant fingerprinting, reservation autocorrect, and graded-throttle playbook
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: After the 2026-02-18 dedicated cluster incident we observed recurring transient saturation events driven by a small set of tenant workloads with highly bursty KV-cache/sequence patterns. This ticket authors a playbook and implementation plan for: (1) deterministic noisy-tenant fingerprinting, (2) reservation autocorrect heuristics to reduce mismatch between declared and effective usage, and (3) graded throttling (multi-step soft-shed) to avoid hard evictions while protecting neighbors.

Goals: Reduce eviction rate and tail latency for shared Dedicated pools; automatically correct reservation sizing drift; provide an operator-friendly runbook and simulation harness to validate config changes without customer impact.

Approach overview:
- Fingerprinting: derive per-tenant signatures from combined features: token-per-second distribution, KV cache churn rate, KV hit/miss ratio, short-sequence spike frequency, and model-variant footprint. Use a rolling 48h baseline and detect >5x deviation on a robust median-based anomaly detector.
- Reservation autocorrect: when sustained deviation (>10% above reservation for 30m and >25% peak bursts) is detected, propose a corrective reservation delta calculated with a safety multiplier (1.15) and a cooldown window (2h) before enforcement. Provide a manually reviewable change in the console before automatic enforcement when customer SLA tier is "enterprise".
- Graded throttling: implement 4-tier soft-shed: observe -> nudge (limit concurrent runs) -> token-rate cap (per-tenant TPS) -> reduced KV allocation (evictable cache slice) -> hard-evict fallback. Each stage triggers only if preceding stage fails to restore headroom within configured threshold.
- Telemetry & simulation: extend dedicated telemetry pipeline to emit per-tenant 1s, 1m, 5m aggregates and synthetic spike injection support in the simulator to validate the autocorrect logic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Telemetry dashboard shows fingerprint classification for >=95% of active tenants in a pool.
- Simulation runbook demonstrates eviction reduction >=40% on representative night-of-incident workload.
- Autocorrect proposals are visible in Console (readable audit trail + PR link) and respect enterprise opt-out.
- Graded throttle states are telemetry-emittable and reversible via console kill-switch.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change billing semantics or permanent reservation contracts; it focuses on technical autocorrect and soft-throttle only.
comments: 2026-02-26 — Kickoff: initial triage with SRE, Runtime, and Customer Success. Agreed to prioritize quick wins (fingerprinting + telemetry) ahead of automatic enforcement. Action: SRE to provide sample spike traces from incident (INC-2026-02-18-DED01). — Liam Chen

2026-03-02 — Prototype fingerprinting: added KV churn and short-sequence spike counters to the collector. Early results: 3 tenants account for 72% of 90th->99th percentile delta across two clusters. See dashboard link. — Maria Gonzalez

2026-03-05 — Design review: PM and Legal flagged the need for console-visible audit trail before any auto-resize for paid customers. We inserted the enterprise opt-out and manual-approve path. — Asha Kapoor

2026-03-08 — Simulation: ran 1000 synthetic spikes against the staging allocator with autocorrect toggled. Results: eviction events reduced by 46% but median latency increased slightly (+3%) under extreme sustained spikes; we'll tune the safety multiplier. PR drafted: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2418 — Liam Chen

2026-03-12 — Security review: KMS changes not required; telemetry contains tenant IDs but will be access-restricted in Console. Security requested retention policy note; updated runbook. — Priya Menon
